verdict.line: You lose if you stand in extended melee trades and let him land three hits for Darkness Rise or get isolated by his R; you win by walling him out of fights and chipping him down with E from range.

brief.thesis: Mordekaiser's kit rewards sustained single-target contact — Obliterate hits hardest on one target, Indestructible banks every point of damage dealt or taken into a shield he can convert to healing, and Realm of Death isolates you for a stat-stealing kill. Yorick doesn't out-trade that directly, but Dark Procession can wall him away from drawn-out fights before his passive or ult come online, which is why this sits at 48.1% over 1122 games rather than clearly lost.

theirWindow.when: after he lands 3 hits on you
theirWindow.what: Darkness Rise triggers a damage aura and move speed burst. Disengage the trade immediately instead of trying to out-auto him here — you lose that exchange.

yourWindow.when: right after his Q or E is spent
yourWindow.what: Obliterate (8-4s cooldown) and Death's Grasp (16-8s cooldown) are both down. Step in, land Q (Last Rites) for the bonus damage and heal, then back out before he resets.

powerCurve.note: both kits weak, neither has a real threat yet

start.why: Measured as the top start at 51.4% over 632 games. The regen and close-range damage reduction offset the chip from his melee Obliterate pokes during early trades.

boots.why: Best-performing boots at 51% over 802 games. Magic resist blunts his full physical-into-magic damage profile, and tenacity shortens how long Death's Grasp pulls you into his follow-up.

core.why: First item in the highest-winrate path (56.9% over 58 games). The damage and move speed spike is what lets you contest him in a straight fight once it's up.
Second in the same path. Armor shred keeps your Q-reset trades relevant as his Indestructible shield grows from tanking your damage.
Completes the top build path. Cooldown reduction means more Q (Last Rites) resets per trade window, which is where your sustain actually comes from.

situational.when: he's building magic resist or kiting your walls with move speed
he's landing Realm of Death on you consistently and you need to survive the isolation
the game drags and his sustained magic damage is outpacing your healing
the lane stabilizes even and you want to convert into a side-lane split-push threat

runes.keystoneWhy: Adaptive damage and healing that ramps over a fight directly counters his Indestructible shield-to-heal loop — you need sustained output across the trade, not one burst, to out-value what he banks.
runes.alternative: Master-tier Yorick players run Grasp of the Undying (Resolve) instead, across 5,865 games — better suited if you're playing this matchup as a tankier wall-and-wait lane rather than trying to out-trade him.

summoners.why: Teleport is the most-picked combo (50.4% pick) and fits the split-push plan this matchup rewards once you have Trinity Force up. Ignite has the higher measured winrate (52.1%) if you'd rather punish his overextensions directly and deny the Indestructible heal on a kill.

playing.title: Count his hits, not just his cooldowns
playing.detail: Darkness Rise needs 3 landed attacks or spells on you. Disengage before the third one connects — the damage aura and speed boost that follow turn an even trade into a loss.

playing.title: Wall him out of his own E pull
playing.detail: If Death's Grasp pulls you in, drop Dark Procession to trap him inside the wall before Darkness Rise can activate, then walk away. This is the single highest-value defensive play in the matchup.

playing.title: Poke with E, don't melee-trade blind
playing.detail: Mourning Mist's armor reduction and slow let you chip him down at range without eating free autos that feed his passive.

playing.title: Close kills by trapping, not chasing
playing.detail: Once he's low, use Dark Procession to wall him in rather than auto-attacking him down — he can't walk through it, and you avoid trading into his last Indestructible shield charge.

playing.title: Never take his Realm of Death alone without an answer
playing.detail: His R isolates you 1v1 and steals your stats permanently on a kill. Only accept that duel when your combat items (Trinity Force, Sterak's) are online or you have a wall already down.

playing.title: Sit on Q resets after every exchange
playing.detail: Last Rites' cooldown drops to 4s by level 18 — always get the bonus-damage hit and heal off after a trade rather than walking away empty-handed.

playing.title: Shift to side-lane pressure once items are up
playing.detail: Since his solo-kill ceiling stays relevant all game, your better path from mid-game on is split-pushing with wall-zoning rather than forcing extended 1v1s.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade timing are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: If pulled by his (E), use [W] to trap him inside to retreat before his (P) activates. Use [E] to poke and [W] to trap him inside when he is running low on health to kill him.
